performance.verdict: CPL crisis is real; Google dead weight and GBP collapse compound Meta's efficiency loss.

findings.text: CPL rose 30.17% week-over-week to ~$16.49 average; 3-day lead total (Sep 14–16) is 16 vs 22 prior 3 days — efficiency and volume both deteriorating together.
5 OVERDUE SOW milestones (earliest Jul 20): Stripe QA, GHL gap closure, end-to-end stack re-test, paid landing pages, and UGC batch — all blocking scale and attribution.
Google Ads has spent $501.02 over 28 days and recorded 0 conversions and only 109 clicks — confirmed non-contributing channel; $7.95–$31.93/day leaking with zero return.
GBP actions collapsed 95% week-over-week (54 actions over 28 days, last 3 days show 0 each); call rate 0.99% — organic local intent has effectively vanished.
GHL shows 154 opportunities created but 0 won and 0 appointments in 28 days — leads are arriving but pipeline intake is not converting, pointing to a CRM/intake process leak, not an ads problem.

suggestions.text: Pause Google Ads entirely — $501.02 spent, 0 conversions, 0 qualified leads over 28 days confirms dead weight.
suggestions.monday_update: Google Ads has spent $501.02 over the past 28 days and produced exactly 0 conversions and 0 leads across 109 clicks. Pause all Google Ads campaigns immediately and redirect the ~$10–$82/day in daily Google spend to Meta, where all 133 leads over the same period originated. Success check: Meta daily spend increases by the reallocated amount by Sep 19, and CPL returns below $13 (its pre-decline baseline) within 7 days. Re-evaluate Google only after paid landing pages are live (overdue SOW milestone).

suggestions.text: Shift Google's ~$18/day average to Meta — keep total spend flat, improve CPL by concentrating budget on the only working channel.
suggestions.monday_update: Meta is the sole lead-generating channel (133 leads / 28 days at $16.49 CPL), while Google has generated 0 leads on $501.02. Move Google's average daily allocation (~$18/day) into Meta to defend lead volume without increasing total spend. Confirm the shift by Sep 19. Success is measured by Meta daily spend rising to ~$90–$95/day and CPL trending back toward $12–$13 by Sep 24 — re-check at that date.

suggestions.text: Escalate GHL intake leak: 154 opportunities, 0 won, 0 appointments — confirm pipeline stages and automation triggers are firing correctly.
suggestions.monday_update: GHL shows 154 opportunities created with 0 won and 0 appointments booked in 28 days — leads are entering the CRM but no downstream action is occurring. This must be diagnosed alongside the overdue end-to-end stack re-test (due Aug 31, still open): check that automation triggers, appointment booking links, and follow-up sequences are firing on new contacts. Success is confirmed when at least one end-to-end test contact moves from created opportunity to appointment within the current workflow, verified by Nacer/Ahmed by Sep 24.
